title: Transition-kind predicate
statement: For a finite Turing machine $M$, a gate kind consists of a machine case, a Boolean flag, and an expectation. On an assignment of Boolean values to the ports, the predicate is true exactly when the guard for that case and flag is false, or the value at the new-bit port equals the bit prescribed by the case’s machine action and expectation.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
A gate kind and a Boolean assignment to its ports
caveat: The snippet does not define the guard, machine action, or expected-bit functions, so their meanings cannot be made more specific from the supplied ground truth.
